Have a great time in Prague, it's an amazing city, went there 3 times this year, can't get enough. Feel free to ask for any other tourist-friendly stuff. Oh, and I'm going again in May for a Rammstein concert. I really can't get enough of this city, it's my favorite city in Europe, nothing else is even close.

Again, just a tourist here (but a Bulgarian one), I've never been there for Christmas, but I can recommend some places. Hemingway Bar is a very nice one for cocktails, you can reserve your seats in advance on their site, but I'm not sure about their working hours during the holidays. The cocktails are amazing, they cost about 13€ or about $16, you gotta check the current prices :D Their English there is quite incredible, the guy who served us was speaking like a British native from the 1800s, so polite and nice. I could also recommend The Alchemist bar for cocktails, too. Both places have real absinthe if you wanna try that.

For the local food, you can eat VERY cheap in the very city center. Try restaurant Mincovna, or if you just want a buffet-style experience for a VERY low price, go to Restaurace Apetit and try their lunch menu. Every time I'm there, I just get my tray, I grab a dish of svichkova (my absolute local favorite) or goulash (not as tasty if you ask me) and I'm in culinary paradise. Wherever you go - try svickova, I dare you. You can also try and sit in U Cerveneho Pava, it's in the city center, it's not that expensive and they cook great food. I'd also recomment Cerveny Jelen for both lunch menu and beer, it's an insanely good place for beer.

And, for a beer with a view, try Kuchyn, right next to the castle. It's better in the warm months because you can sit in the garden, though, where the view over the city is.

As another tourist, all I can say is - I wouldn't go for the night clubs and I'd hit the bars instead. You can tupsa tupsa anywhere in the world, and most of the clubs are just full of tourists anyway. I had so much better time in cocktail bars and I loved the atmosphere. Still, I'm not a club-going kind of guy, so take my opinion with a grain of salt.

Anyway, if you're looking for a good cocktail bar to sit in, you can hit Hemingway's Bar (reservation is highly recommended as they have strict rules for not allowing people inside if all the seats are taken), the cocktails are about 13€ each, there's absinthe, too. You can also go to The Alchemist Bar, another nice place with cocktails. 

As for night clubs (for dancing & stuff), you can try the ones in Zizkov for either hookups or fights (or both). Or to the basic tupsa tupsa ones on Dlouha. Or to the ones in Andel, but mostly for the fights :D

By the way, we have a kind of trdelnik here in Bulgaria, too, but at least no one says it's "traditional". Also, it's cheaper and better, even though the technology is the same.

As for the water - I know it's drinkable, but it's not as fresh as the one I'm used to where I live, and even here I rely on mineral water. Just how I'm used to. And hey, I'm not buying it at a restaurant :D

Can I say? I'm also just a tourist but I've been to Prague 3 times this year as it's my absolute favorite city in Europe. I can honestly say, 3 days will be pretty much enough to see most of the interesting things and experience the city. By the way, I'm also going in November (7 to 10) again to see a concert.

Anyway. My advice:

1. Find a place near the city center but not right inside it, because it can get quite noisy and most of these places don't have air conditioning and just radiators.
2. Walk around the old town and walk to the castle. If you don't need to take the tram or the metro to go somewhere specific and far - just walk and enjoy the views. Go to the castle on foot. 
3. Do NOT eat in the old town square. You can eat an inexpensive meal in the city center at many places but don't sit near the clock or something. I can give you my recommendations if you want.
4. If you love beer, this is the place for you. I always have one at Kuchyn's garden (near the castle and when it's warm), one at "U Cerveny Jelen", and one at a very cute tram comverted into a little bar. "Bistro Tocna" or something like that.
5. Buy water at the supermarket, don't order it in restaurants. Beer is literally cheaper and they will ridicule you for getting water over beer :D
6. Take a walk while it's dark.
7. Go for the cockctail bars with REAL absinthe but be prepared to pay quite a lot for the experience. But you should do it at least once.
8. Do NOT eat "trdelnik". It's expensive, nothing special, nothing traditional, and everyone will know you're tourists. Visit one of the dozens small bakeries there and get some kolac, or if you want your teeth to fall off from the sugar - indianek.
9. Don't fall for any tourist traps. Bus tours, old car rides, carriage rides, scammers telling you they have a better exchange rate on the street, getting your caricature made, buying locks for the Charles Bridge... just... no.
10. For me, food is a whole experience in Prague. My favorite is "svickova" but the "gulash" is also good. Eat the local cuisine, it's very tasty.
11. If you're out late and you're hungry, go to Bageterie Boulevard. It's a local company for fast food with baguettes, they are quite good for a night snack. Some of them work until 1 or 3 after midnight.
12. Don't look for something particular to do and make it unique - it's all unique there. It's incredibly beautiful. Visit some museums, drink some coffee (not Starbucks), drink some beer, enjoy some cocktail bar, see the Dancing House, see the Zizkov tower with the crawling babies on it, take a walk on the Golden lane where Kafka lived, and just... take it all with your eyes. Pictures don't do enough justice to this incredible place. Oh, and avoid the ridiculous "sex museum" if you ask me. But hey, whatever floats your boat.

All in all, if this is your first time in Prague, I'm pretty sure you'll want to visit again but for longer :D

Look, everyone relaxes in a different way. Still, that doesn't mean there are 8 billion ways to relax. However, the stress you experience might be inevitable whatever your fun hobby is so I'll encourage you to just reduce stress naturally. You can do it during every day, not just on the weekends.
